Dualities emerge in how simulations encode uncertainty—either through ensemble averaging or probabilistic bounds. Failure modes arise when models lack sufficient expressiveness or when data-driven inference assumes independence or stationarity that does not hold. These primitives form a hierarchical architecture: modeling provides abstraction layers, simulation enables dynamic exploration, and decision systems operationalize insights. Each layer introduces potential sources of error—epistemic uncertainty in modeling, aleatoric noise in simulation, and strategic misalignment in decision-making. The interplay of these components defines the robustness of computational science frameworks.
